hypothesis: RUNTIME surface, additive observability: classify model-call failures at the ovp-llm boundary (`ovp_llm::failure_class(&CallError) -> &'static str`, stable wire vocabulary auth | rate_limited | context_exceeded | budget_exhausted | overloaded | network | decode | protocol | cache_miss | provider_error | internal) and carry the slug through the agent so surfaces can show a TARGETED fix hint instead of a bare 'model call failed'. Three additive carriers: (1) TranscriptEvent::ModelFailed gains `class` (serde default — old transcripts read back with class=""), (2) AgentOutcome gains `failure_class: Option<&'static str>` (Some only on stopped_reason=model_error; None on idempotent replays — the class lives in the audit transcript, replay does not re-derive it), (3) POST /api/ask response body gains `failure_class` and the portal maps the six actionable slugs to bilingual hints (auth → check providers.toml key; rate_limited/overloaded → retry later; context_exceeded → new chat or narrow the question; budget_exhausted → retry/simplify; network → check connectivity/proxy) while unactionable slugs fall back to the existing generic stop note. Classification is code, not judge: the ground truth (HTTP status + Anthropic error code + CallError variant) is decidable, so per the decidability rule this is a match arm, not a prompt. Motivated by the 2026-08-03 crystallize incident class (a swallowed raw error) and the Cabinet research verdict that adapter-level error classification is the highest-value borrow.

predicted_delta.operational_reliability: an ask turn that dies on an expired key now tells the operator to fix providers.toml instead of showing 'model call failed'; retryable-vs-config-fix is distinguishable at a glance in the portal and in the audit transcript

guardrails.additive_only: no existing field changes meaning; ModelFailed.class deserializes old transcripts via serde default; AgentOutcome remains PartialEq; /api/ask emits failure_class: null except on model_error
guardrails.replay_honesty: idempotent replays report failure_class=None rather than re-deriving — replay never fabricates execution artifacts (same rule as coverage=null on replay)
guardrails.classification_is_total: failure_class is a total function over CallError — every variant maps to a slug, unknown provider codes land in provider_error, never a panic or empty string from the live path
guardrails.hint_scope: the portal maps ONLY the six actionable slugs to hints; decode/protocol/internal keep the generic stop note (no fabricated advice for caller bugs)

tests: ovp-llm client::retry_tests::failure_class_covers_the_wire_vocabulary — the full slug vocabulary against numeric HTTP codes, the no_api_key sentinel, structured provider types, and every non-Provider variant
ovp-memory agent::tests::model_failure_ends_turn_honestly — extended: outcome.failure_class=Some("network") and the ModelFailed audit event carries class="network"
console-ui typecheck + vitest (failureHintKey wiring compiles against the MsgKey union — a slug without i18n keys is a build error)
eval_plan.live_check: next real ask failure in the portal shows the targeted hint line under the stop note; the session transcript's model_failed event carries the class

rollback: revert the commit; transcript compatibility is two-way (older builds ignore the unknown `class` field on read, newer builds read old lines as class="" via serde default)
